authoritative_for: Bazaar owns exact string content and append-only per-ID versions, its local read/write API, database initialization, and program installation.

Bazaar owns shared prompt selections, exact component loading, one-pass rendering, trusted reference and description expansion, numeric selection-version compatibility helpers, and explicit reviewed prompt imports.
not_authoritative_for: Products own authored meaning, runtime inputs, model and permission choices, schema and tool structure, tool implementations, request assembly, domain results, and recovery. Generic raw strings retain caller-owned formats and meaning.

covers: All public string reads, version-history reads, appends, prompt preparation and imports, initialization, integrity checks, and program installation/recovery outcomes.
excludes: Help/version, implementation helpers, model configuration interpretation, request execution, caller migration, domain interpretation, and arbitrary direct SQL access.

shared_access_and_trust: The current user owns private local state. The Rust API operates in process. Agent readers have read-only database access; explicit writers append. No daemon, network listener, or application-level authentication is supplied.
shared_privacy_and_retention: Content and IDs may be sensitive. Every committed version is retained without automatic deletion. CLI command usage recording omits arguments and content and preserves results after recording errors.
compatibility_and_retirement: String versions, database schema one, JSON output schema one, prompt import and selection formats one, capability versions, requester identities, and product releases are independent. Ordinary CLI output is readable text by default; explicit --json retains the existing success and operational-error envelopes. Raw Rust API types and behavior remain unchanged. Unsupported or foreign state fails without automatic migration. Historical prompt selections and components remain retained.
operational_limits: Each append changes one ID. Reads of different IDs have separate snapshots. Prompt publication places components before complete per-owner selections and provides no atomic all-requester cutover. Bazaar stores whole strings and imports whole documents; no capacity, throughput or latency guarantee is supplied.
